memos.risk:
Refuse at any size. This brief has several gaps that matter. Class is UNRESOLVED, so I can't tell whether this is a factory, operator-backed, or a random launch. Bundle share, buyer concentration on the curve, and graduation delay are all null, so the one check that separates operator-backed coins from factory coins is missing. Name, symbol, and metadata are null too, so there's nothing to read.

The numbers that exist don't settle it. Pool depth of about 85 SOL is thin, so a $20 round trip would eat well above the low end of the 1.4-5.1% fee range. The 15-minute window shows heavy churn: sells of 144 SOL against buys of 189, with net flow of only 45 SOL and a 2.7x return that could be a short-lived spike. The 11% drawdown from the 30-minute high suggests the move is already fading.

If the desk later gets bundle share, buyer concentration, and a resolved class showing operator backing, I'd reconsider a $5 ticket with a 25% stop and a 15-30 minute hold. Without those, skip.
memos.scout:
Case for buying: The last 15 minutes show real two-sided activity: 269 buyers and 198 sellers, 188.9 SOL bought against 143.8 SOL sold, and net inflow of 45 SOL, so demand is still absorbing supply rather than just exiting. The price is up 272% over the window (return 2.72) and sits only 11% below its 30-minute high, which means it has held most of its gains through the pullback. Its first two minutes were broad, with 166 buyers, a top-5 buyer share of just 25%, and no airdrop dump seen. The pool is 85 SOL deep, enough to keep the round-trip cost near the lower end of the range.

Weak points: the first-two-minutes sell-to-buy ratio of 1.02 and the launch bot are warning signs, the graduation timing and curve data are missing, and the name and symbol are null, so there is no way to check the metadata. Net flow is only modestly positive against a large gross volume. A 30-60 minute hold would need the net inflow to persist. Honest call: a thin case, and the missing fields argue for skipping unless the desk accepts that uncertainty.
memos.skeptic:
Most likely loss path: a dump by early holders after a run. The coin is up 2.72x over the last 15 minutes, but 143.83 SOL was sold against 188.88 bought, and 198 sellers against 269 buyers. That's heavy distribution into a rally, and sell-to-buy in the first two minutes was already 1.02 (75.47 SOL bought, 76.6 sold) with a launch bot present. Net flow is still positive (+45 SOL), but that is recent momentum money that can reverse fast. The 11.2% drawdown from the 30-minute high suggests the top is already being sold.

Fees matter too: the pool is only 84.96 SOL deep, so a 1.4-5.1% round trip plus impact can erase a modest bounce. The return over 30 minutes is just +3.5%, so there's little cushion.

Missing data (bundle share, completer share, metadata, name, symbol, graduation timing) means we can't rule out insider supply. Unresolved class with blank fields argues for skipping.
